chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Whoever learns knowledge and acts by it and teaches for God's sake will be called magnificent in the kingdom of the heavens, and it will be said: He learned for God, and he acted for God, and he taught for God.'

key_terms.تَعَلَّمَ: To learn, to acquire knowledge — the first stage of the scholarly vocation
key_terms.عَظِيمًا: Magnificent, great — the honorific title bestowed in the heavenly realm
key_terms.عَلَّمَ لِلَّهِ: To teach for God's sake — transmission of knowledge purely for the divine purpose
key_terms.عَمِلَ بِهِ: To act upon it — putting knowledge into practice
key_terms.مَلَكُوتِ السَّمَاوَاتِ: Kingdom of the heavens — the spiritual realm beyond the material world

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Sadiq say about one who learns, acts, and teaches for God's sake?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that sincerity of purpose elevates a scholar to a position of greatness in the celestial realm. The hadith identifies three inseparable dimensions of the sacred scholarly vocation — learning, practicing, and transmitting — all conditioned upon sincerity (ikhlas) for God's sake alone. The audience of Imam al-Sadiq's time would have understood this as a rebuke of scholars who sought worldly gain through knowledge, contrasting them with the truly righteous scholar whose title 'magnificent' (azim) is proclaimed in the heavens.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood Al Minqary, from Hafs Bin Giyas who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The one who learns the knowledge and acts by it, and teaches for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> (without taking payment for the worldly needs) would be called as ‘عَظِيماً’ the magnificent in kingdom of the skies, so it would be said: ‘He learnt it for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and acted for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and taught for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!’’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari from Hafs ibn Ghiyath who has said that abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said the following.

“Whoever acquires knowledge and practice what he has learned and teach it to others for the sake of Allah, among the angels of heavens he will be called a great personality. It will be said there: ‘He learned for the sake of Allah, practiced for the sake of Allah and taught it for the sake of Allah.”
